title: The invention of karaoke: Daisuke Inoue's 1971 machine for Kobe bars, the earlier Sparko Box, and why neither inventor patented it

facts.text: Daisuke Inoue was born in Osaka in 1940 and took up the drums at Osaka Technical High School.
By 1970, Inoue and six other musicians were playing in clubs in Kobe; he backed customers who wanted to sing.
Inoue could not read music; he learned to follow singers by watching their lips.
The president of a small steel company asked Inoue for a tape of his playing so he could sing on an overnight trip to a hot spring, and Inoue made one.
Inoue reasoned that if company presidents could sing to taped music, ordinary people in small bars could too.
Inoue and his friends had 11 home-built machines made, with amplifiers and specially made tapes, and began leasing them to bars in Kobe in 1971.
Inoue's machine was called the 8 Juke; it was based on a car stereo and helped make karaoke a business.
Inoue recorded backing tracks of pop songs in keys that ordinary amateur singers could manage.
Inoue did not patent his machine, and electronics companies soon began making and selling their own versions.
The only patent Inoue ever held, and only briefly, was for plastic-covered songbooks; he made almost no money from karaoke.
The word karaoke literally means 'empty orchestra' in Japanese.
Shigeichi Negishi of Tokyo built a coin-operated sing-along machine called the Sparko Box in 1967 and sold around 8,000 of them.
Negishi never patented the Sparko Box either; the Japanese karaoke industry group credits several people who built machines independently in the late 1960s and early 1970s.
By the 1980s, karaoke boxes with private rooms had spread across Japan and replaced bars as the main places to sing.
In 2022 Japan had more than 8,000 karaoke box venues, and 131,500 bars had karaoke machines.
Inoue did not sing karaoke himself until his 59th birthday in 1999.
In 2004 Inoue won the Ig Nobel Peace Prize for inventing karaoke, which the prize said gave people a new way to learn to tolerate each other.
Video karaoke and networked karaoke systems later helped karaoke spread across Asia and the rest of the world.

notes: 批次指定角度說井上大佑 1971 年做出「第一台」伴唱機；來源（CNN、NPR 2024）指出根岸重一 1967 年的 Sparko Box 更早，日本卡拉 OK 產業團體不把發明歸給單一個人。選文應寫成井上「讓卡拉 OK 流行起來」、並交代另有更早的機器，不寫成「世界第一台」。
